summary: The investigation could not definitively identify a root cause; the leading hypothesis (downstream market-data-service latency increase) has low confidence (0.28). Verified observations confirm a sharp latency rise in pricing-engine starting at 13:18‑13:22 with stable CPU and no recent deployments, but missing downstream and network metrics prevent ruling out other causes.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Downstream market-data-service latency increase
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A latency spike in market-data-service caused pricing-engine calls to take longer, inflating its p99 latency.

causal_chain.claim: market-data-service experienced increased response latency around 13:18
pricing-engine observed p99 latency rise to >2 s

assumptions: market-data-service latency metrics would show a spike at 13:18
no other downstream service caused the delay

ranked_hypotheses.title: Redis-cache resource exhaustion causing request delays
ranked_hypotheses.statement: High load or contention on the shared redis-cache increased request latency for pricing-engine, leading to degraded quote times.

causal_chain.claim: redis-cache experienced high latency or connection pool exhaustion around 13:18
pricing-engine observed p99 latency rise to >2 s

assumptions: redis-cache latency metrics would show a spike at 13:18
pricing-engine reliance on redis-cache is significant for quote generation

ranked_hypotheses.title: Network congestion between pricing-engine and its dependencies
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A transient network issue increased round‑trip times to downstream services, causing pricing-engine latency to jump.

causal_chain.claim: network latency or packet loss increased for traffic to market-data-service and redis-cache around 13:18
pricing-engine observed p99 latency rise to >2 s

assumptions: network monitoring would show elevated latency or errors at the time
no other infrastructure component (e.g., load balancer) failed

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared library regression introduced via a recent deployment
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A recent deployment of a shared library used by pricing-engine introduced a performance regression, causing higher processing latency.

causal_chain.claim: a deployment of a shared library (used by pricing-engine) occurred shortly before 13:18 and introduced slower code paths
pricing-engine observed p99 latency rise to >2 s

assumptions: the shared library deployment is not recorded in pricing-engine's own deployment history
no other service deployments occurred that could explain the latency

facts.statement: Pricing-engine p99 latency sharply increased at 2026-04-09T13:22:00Z, jumping from ~60 ms to >2 s.
After the onset, pricing-engine p99 latency stayed elevated (≈1.8‑2.2 s) through the observation window.
Coarser 6‑minute buckets confirm the latency surge beginning at the 13:18 bucket (max ≈ 2.2 s) and remaining high thereafter.
CPU usage for pricing-engine stayed around 38‑41 % with no noticeable spike during the latency degradation.
No deployments were recorded for pricing-engine between 2026-04-09T12:00:00Z and 2026-04-09T14:00:00Z.
No configuration changes were recorded for pricing-engine in the same window.
The service dependency graph shows pricing-engine calls market-data-service (http) and redis-cache (cache).
Redis-cache is a shared datastore used by multiple services including pricing-engine and market-data-service.
No deployments were recorded for any service in the window 2026-04-09T12:00:00Z to 2026-04-09T14:00:00Z.

assumptions: market-data-service latency metrics would show a spike at 13:18
no other downstream service caused the delay

timeline.event: Coarse latency bucket indicates start of surge (max ≈2.2 s).
Pricing-engine p99 latency spikes sharply (>2 s).
Incident reported by on‑call SRE; alerts fire (deadline‑exceeded).

recommended_actions.action: Collect and examine latency metrics for market-data-service and redis-cache for the window 13:00‑14:00 UTC.
recommended_actions.rationale: Missing downstream latency data is a key gap; confirming or refuting spikes will discriminate between H1 and H2.

recommended_actions.action: Run network health checks (e.g., ping, traceroute, packet loss) between pricing-engine and its downstream services.
recommended_actions.rationale: Network congestion is hypothesis H3; direct measurement will clarify if network latency contributed.

recommended_actions.action: Enable detailed request tracing (e.g., OpenTelemetry) for pricing-engine calls to market-data-service and redis-cache.
recommended_actions.rationale: Will provide per‑request latency breakdown to pinpoint the slow path.

recommended_actions.action: Query deployment and configuration change history for downstream services (market-data-service, redis-cache, exchange-gateway, order-service, api-gateway) for the incident window.
recommended_actions.rationale: Addresses gaps that could reveal a hidden change supporting H1, H2, H3, or H4.

recommended_actions.action: Restart pricing-engine pods to clear any potential in‑process state or resource contention.
recommended_actions.rationale: Safe mitigation; if latency drops, suggests transient internal issue.

recommended_actions.action: Add alerting on downstream service latency (market-data-service, redis-cache) and on network RTTs.
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents recurrence by surfacing similar latency spikes early.

recommended_actions.action: Implement version‑aware deployment tracking for shared libraries and enforce audit of any library updates.
recommended_actions.rationale: Mitigates risk of hidden shared‑library regressions (H4).

data_gaps: Missing error_rate metric for pricing-engine; cannot correlate errors with latency.
Latency metrics for downstream services (market-data-service, redis-cache, exchange-gateway, etc.) were not retrieved.
Network latency and packet loss measurements between pricing-engine and its dependencies are absent.
Deployment and configuration change history for downstream services is unavailable.
Historical incident data for similar pricing-engine latency patterns was not searched.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Observation of a clear latency spike in market-data-service at ~13:18‑13:22 would raise confidence in H1.
Observation of a latency spike or high contention metrics in redis-cache at the same time would support H2.
Network monitoring showing elevated RTTs or packet loss between pricing-engine and its dependencies would support H3.
Discovery of a recent shared‑library deployment affecting pricing-engine would support H4.

findings.statement: Pricing-engine p99 latency sharply increased at 2026-04-09T13:22:00Z, jumping from ~60 ms to >2 s.
After the onset, pricing-engine p99 latency stayed elevated (≈1.8‑2.2 s) through the observation window.
Coarser 6‑minute buckets confirm the latency surge beginning at the 13:18 bucket (max ≈ 2.2 s) and remaining high thereafter.
CPU usage for pricing-engine stayed around 38‑41 % with no noticeable spike during the latency degradation.
No deployments were recorded for pricing-engine between 2026-04-09T12:00:00Z and 2026-04-09T14:00:00Z.
No configuration changes were recorded for pricing-engine in the same window.

The service dependency graph (depth 2) shows pricing-engine calls market-data-service (http) and redis-cache (cache); order-service calls pricing-engine (http); market-data-service also calls redis-cache (cache) and exchange-gateway (http); api-gateway calls order-service (http).
Redis-cache is a shared datastore used by multiple services (pricing-engine, market-data-service, etc.).
No deployments were recorded for any service (all services scope) in the window 2026-04-09T12:00:00Z to 2026-04-09T14:00:00Z.
